D-01.title: Design: A/R Summary at 1440 px in light theme looks as described

fields.title: Design: A/R Summary at 1440 px in light theme looks as described
fields.custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • Scenario: Your shop works at two locations, and you check how A/R Summary looks in light theme, next to Sales By Customer.
  • You are an Admin user (the "Admin" role) working at {Location-A}, your current location.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The organization has open documents in these reports at two locations, {Location-A} and {Location-B}, and you are enrolled at both; {Location-A}'s name comes first in A to Z order.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and {Location-B} is Staging Lethbridge - 4310.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has a long name (more than 40 characters) and open documents at both locations on today's date, including a credit memo.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST D-01 Northern Alberta Heavy Equipment and Trailer Repair.
  • Starting screen: A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu in light theme at 100% zoom.
  • Sales By Customer (Reports, then "Sales By Customer" under PERFORMANCE in the left menu) is open in a second tab of the same window, for comparison.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
fields.custom_steps:
1. Look at the title row.
  2. Look at where the filter row sits, and compare with Sales By Customer.
  3. Read the column headings left to right, letter for letter, capitals included.
  4. Look for a sideways scroll bar under the table.
  5. Look at {Customer-A}'s name cell and at the money cells.
  6. Look across the whole page for any text that overlaps, is cut off or is clipped.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the title, its info icon directly right of it, and the ⋯ Export button at the right end, all on one line.
  • Step 2: the filter row sits below the title row, in the same place as on Sales By Customer.
  • Step 3: the customer name heading (first column), "Location", "Current", "1-30 Days", "31-60 Days", "61-90 Days", "91 And Over", "Total" ("Location" shown because two locations are in view; it sits right after the name). No heading wraps.
  • Step 4: there is none: every column is visible at 1440 px without scrolling sideways.
  • Step 5: the long name wraps onto a second line; money, date and number cells stay on one line, and Location does not wrap.
  • Step 6: nothing overlaps, is cut off or clipped.

The first column keeps today's heading: only the Location column is renamed in this release.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 9 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11532 (Story 2, Sort by clicking any column header), story SV-11536 (Story 6, Location column), story SV-11538 (Story 8, Report descriptions and layout)

  • S8-R2: “The title, its info icon and the Export menu stay on one line at 1440 pixels wide; the filter row sits below them, positioned as on the native reports.”
  • S8-R3: “The headline column (Open Balance; Total on the Summaries) is pinned to the right edge and bold on the header, every row, every expanded row and the Totals row, as on Sales By Customer. At 1440 pixels wide every column of all six reports is visible without scrolling sideways: the customer or vendor name and Transaction Type wrap long values onto a second line, Location wraps only on A/P Detail (nine columns), column headings never wrap, and money, date and number columns never wrap. Narrower than 1440 pixels, the table scrolls sideways under the pinned column.”
  • S2-R1, A/R Summary and A/P Summary columns: “A/R Summary and A/P Summary: the name column, Location (when shown), Current, 1-30 Days, 31-60 Days, 61-90 Days, 91 And Over, Total.”
  • S2-R4a: “Column headings are in Title Case on all six reports, on screen, in the PDF and in the CSV, as on the other reports (Sales By Customer, Inventory Value, Parts Velocity): the A/R reports read "Transaction Type", "Customer Full Name", "Due Date", "Past Due" and "Open Balance", the same as the A/P reports.”
  • S6-R3: “It sits right after the Date column, before the money columns; on A/R Summary and A/P Summary, which have no Date column, right after the customer or vendor name.”
  • Key Decisions, reuse rule: “The reuse rule. Every control on these reports reuses an existing ShopView pattern: the native filter chips, the native totals row and pinned headline column of the newer reports, the existing location-switch prompt, the design system's chevron icon. Nothing new is drawn. Basis: d-reuse-existing-pattern.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), read 22 Oct 2026: page 1 "Opening order and header sorting" (board Main.dc.html); page 6 "Descriptions and pinned column" (board Layout.dc.html). Compare the screen with the pictures below at 100% zoom; the expected results still come from the PRD quotes above, the pictures give the look and the on-screen labels.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • ar-ap-p1-a-r-aging-summary-opens-a-to-z.png: figure "A/R Aging Summary opens A to Z" (This build (after)), board "1. Opening order and header sorting"
  • ar-ap-p1-click-the-total-header.png: figure "Click the Total header" (This build (after)), board "1. Opening order and header sorting"
  • ar-ap-p6-a-p-detail-scrolled-sideways-light.png: figure "A/P Detail scrolled sideways, light" (Production (before)), board "6. Report descriptions and the pinned headline column" (today's look, for comparison only)

The design's own words:

  • "Customer name order the way QuickBooks sorts ("10 Trucking" before "2 Trucking"), marked on the Customer header. S1-R1, S1-R2, S1-R4, S1-R7, S1-R8." (caption of "A/R Aging Summary opens A to Z")
  • "First click gives the useful order: money largest first. Second click reverses, third repeats the first. S2-R1, S2-R2, S2-R3, S2-R7." (caption of "Click the Total header")
  • "No description anywhere; no column stays in place." (caption of "A/P Detail scrolled sideways, light")

  • Step 5: the focused link is underlined.
  • Step 6: nothing overlaps, is cut off or is hard to read.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 9 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location), story SV-11537 (Story 7, Document links open where they can), story SV-11538 (Story 8, Report descriptions and layout)

  • S7-R7: “Links use the native report link style (the same blue as Work In Progress, semi-bold, no underline, underlined only on keyboard focus), readable in light and dark theme.”
  • S8-R3: “The headline column (Open Balance; Total on the Summaries) is pinned to the right edge and bold on the header, every row, every expanded row and the Totals row, as on Sales By Customer.   • S8-R4: “The Totals row uses the native totals row style of the newer reports.”
  • S5-R13: “The customer chip (A/R) and vendor chip (A/P) and their open menus are the native ones: Customer exactly as Sales By Customer's Customer filter (person icon), Vendor exactly as Inventory Value's Vendor filter (truck icon, "Search vendors"; as there, the search box shows only when there are more than 8 vendors). The menu has a search box, an "All customers" or "All vendors" row, the native line "All customers are included. Pick one or more to narrow." (or vendors) while none is ticked, and the list; several can be ticked. The chip reads "Customer: All customers" or "Vendor: All vendors" in the resting (grey) style when none is ticked, the name when one is (shortened with "..." when long), and "Customer: N customers" or "Vendor: N vendors" when N are. The ticked customers or vendors narrow every row, group, total, page, sort and export; the Location list does not change (S5-R3).”
  • S5-R15: “The Past due chip and its open menu are the same native checkbox dropdown as Customer and Location: label "Past due", an hourglass icon, an "Any" row, the native line "All ranges are included. Pick one or more to narrow." while none is ticked, then "1-30 days", "31-60 days", "61-90 days", "91+ days", in that order; several can be ticked. The chip reads "Past due: Any" in the resting (grey) style when none is ticked, the range when one is (for example "Past due: 91+ days"), and "Past due: N ranges" when N are. Ticking all four reads "Past due: 4 ranges", not Any, because Any also keeps invoices and bills that are not due yet. Preconditions

  • Customer {Customer-A} has a long name (more than 40 characters) and open documents at both locations on today's date, including a credit memo.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST D-07 Northern Alberta Heavy Equipment and Trailer Repair.
  • Starting screen: A/R Collection (Reports, then "A/R Aging Collection" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu in light theme at 100% zoom, with every group expanded (Expand all).
  • Sales By Customer (Reports, then "Sales By Customer" under PERFORMANCE in the left menu) is open in a second tab of the same window, for comparison.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
fields.custom_steps:
1. Look at the title row.

fields.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the title, its info icon directly right of it, and the ⋯ Export button at the right end, all on one line.
  • Step 2: the filter row sits below the title row, in the same place as on Sales By Customer.
  • Step 3: "Date", "Location", "Transaction Type", "ID", "Due Date", "Past Due", "Amount", "Open Balance" ("Location" shown because two locations are in view; it sits right after "Date"). No heading wraps.
  • Step 4: there is none: every column is visible at 1440 px without scrolling sideways.
  • Step 5: the long name and a long Transaction Type wrap onto a second line; money, date and number cells stay on one line, and Location does not wrap.
  • Step 6: nothing overlaps, is cut off or clipped.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 9 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11532 (Story 2, Sort by clicking any column header), story SV-11536 (Story 6, Location column), story SV-11538 (Story 8, Report descriptions and layout)

  • S8-R2: “The title, its info icon and the Export menu stay on one line at 1440 pixels wide; the filter row sits below them, positioned as on the native reports.”
  • S8-R3: “The headline column (Open Balance; Total on the Summaries) is pinned to the right edge and bold on the header, every row, every expanded row and the Totals row, as on Sales By Customer. At 1440 pixels wide every column of all six reports is visible without scrolling sideways: the customer or vendor name and Transaction Type wrap long values onto a second line, Location wraps only on A/P Detail (nine columns), column headings never wrap, and money, date and number columns never wrap. Narrower than 1440 pixels, the table scrolls sideways under the pinned column.”
  • S2-R1, A/R Collection columns: “A/R Collection: Date, Location (when shown), Transaction Type, ID, Due Date, Past Due, Amount, Open Balance.”
  • S2-R4a: “Column headings are in Title Case on all six reports, on screen, in the PDF and in the CSV, as on the other reports (Sales By Customer, Inventory Value, Parts Velocity): the A/R reports read "Transaction Type", "Customer Full Name", "Due Date", "Past Due" and "Open Balance", the same as the A/P reports.”
  • S6-R3: “It sits right after the Date column, before the money columns; on A/R Summary and A/P Summary, which have no Date column, right after the customer or vendor name.”
  • Key Decisions, reuse rule: “The reuse rule. Every control on these reports reuses an existing ShopView pattern: the native filter chips, the native totals row and pinned headline column of the newer reports, the existing location-switch prompt, the design system's chevron icon. Nothing new is drawn. Basis: d-reuse-existing-pattern.”

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • ar-ap-p3-expand-all-from-the-header.png: figure "Expand all from the header" (This build (after)), board "3. Collapse all, Expand all and pinned group rows"
  • ar-ap-p6-info-icon-beside-the-title-light.png: figure "Info icon beside the title, light" (This build (after)), board "6. Report descriptions and the pinned headline column"
  • ar-ap-p6-a-p-detail-scrolled-sideways-light.png: figure "A/P Detail scrolled sideways, light" (Production (before)), board "6. Report descriptions and the pinned headline column" (today's look, for comparison only)

Difference from the PRD (DD-06), closed: PRD version 5 said A/R Detail and A/R Collection headings written "Transaction type", "Customer full name", "Due date", "Past due", "Open balance" (S2-R1); the design shows the after pictures read "Transaction Type", "Customer Full Name", "Due Date", "Past Due", "Open Balance"; today's production pictures already read the same, with "Location Full Name". Chris Ward ruled on 23 Oct 2026 (answer 4): Title Case on all six reports, on screen, in the PDF and in the CSV, as the design shows; PRD version 9 adds S2-R4a and writes S2-R1 in Title Case. fields.custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • Scenario: A customer's invoices are all at your other location, and you check how A/R Summary looks while loading and when empty.
  • You are an Admin user (the "Admin" role) working at {Location-A}, your current location.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.

    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and {Location-B} is Staging Lethbridge - 4310.

    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST D-19 States.
  • Starting screen: A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu.

fields.custom_steps:
1. Change the as-of date to yesterday and watch the table straight away.
  2. Change the as-of date back to today.
  3. In the Location menu, untick {Location-B}.
  4. In the Customer filter, tick {Customer-A}.
  5. Read the empty state, letter for letter, and compare it with Sales By Customer's empty state.
  6. Click "Clear all filters".
fields.custom_expected:

Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • Scenario: Your shop works at two locations, and you check how the export success and empty-export messages look.
  • You are an Admin user (the "Admin" role) working at {Location-A}, your current location.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The organization has open documents in these reports at two locations, {Location-A} and {Location-B}, and you are enrolled at both; {Location-A}'s name comes first in A to Z order.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and {Location-B} is Staging Lethbridge - 4310.
  • Starting screen: A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu in light theme at 100% zoom.
  • Sales By Customer (Reports, then "Sales By Customer" under PERFORMANCE in the left menu) is open in a second tab of the same window, for comparison.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
fields.custom_steps:
1. Download the CSV from the ⋯ menu and read the message, letter for letter.
  2. Compare it with the message Sales By Customer shows after a CSV download.
  3. In the Location menu, click "Clear selection".
  4. Download the PDF from the ⋯ menu and read the message.
  5. Compare it with Sales By Customer's warning for an empty export.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: "Success", "Data exported successfully."
  • Step 2: the same success message, look and position.
  • Step 3: no location is ticked.
  • Step 4: "Empty export", "Export didn't yield any results"; nothing downloads.
  • Step 5: the same native warning look and position.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 9 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11533 (Story 3, Export to PDF and CSV)

  • User Feedback Summary: “Export succeeds | "Success", "Data exported successfully." | Success toast, as on the other reports”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Export with no rows | "Empty export", "Export didn't yield any results" | Warning toast; nothing downloads”
  • S3-R10: “A successful export shows the native "Success" message, "Data exported successfully." An export with no rows downloads nothing and shows the native warning "Empty export", "Export didn't yield any results".”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), read 22 Oct 2026: page 2 "Export" (board Export.dc.html). The design draws neither the Success message nor the Empty export warning (all 7 boards checked); the case compares with Sales By Customer, as the PRD says.

Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are an Admin user (the "Admin" role) working at {Location-A}, your current location.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The organization has more than 2,000 open A/P lines.
    For example: the QA organization (13,540).
  • You can switch this computer's network connection off and on (for example Wi-Fi).
  • Starting screen: A/P Detail (Reports, then "A/P Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS PAYABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu in light theme at 100% zoom.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
fields.custom_steps:
1. Choose "Download (PDF)" from the ⋯ menu and read the message, letter for letter.
  2. Switch the network connection off.
  3. Choose "Download (CSV)" from the ⋯ menu and read the message, letter for letter.
  4. Switch the network back on.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: "This report is too large for PDF. Export it as CSV, or narrow the filters, then try again.", in an error toast styled and placed as on the other reports, and only one.
  • Step 2: the computer is offline.
  • Step 3: "We couldn't export this report. Please try again.", an error toast, only one.
  • Step 4: the connection is back.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 9 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11533 (Story 3, Export to PDF and CSV)

  • User Feedback Summary: “PDF export over 2,000 rows | "This report is too large for PDF. Export it as CSV, or narrow the filters, then try again." | Error toast, as on the other reports; nothing downloads”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Export fails for any other reason | "We couldn't export this report. Please try again." | Error toast; nothing downloads; these six reports only”
  • S3-N1: “Over 2,000 rows, the PDF is refused before anything is generated: no download, and the message "This report is too large for PDF. Export it as CSV, or narrow the filters, then try again." Exactly 2,000 rows is allowed.”
  • Story 3, Error Handling: “If an export fails for any other reason (a server error or a lost connection), nothing downloads and one error message shows: "We couldn't export this report. Please try again." This message is on these six reports only; the other reports keep theirs.”

D-39.title: Design: the switch-location dialog for a work order looks as described

fields.title: Design: the switch-location dialog for a work order looks as described
fields.custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • Scenario: A customer has a work order invoice made at your other location, and you check how the switch-location prompt looks.
  • You are an Admin user (the "Admin" role) working at {Location-A}, your current location.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The organization has open documents in these reports at two locations, {Location-A} and {Location-B}, and you are enrolled at both; {Location-A}'s name comes first in A to Z order.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and {Location-B} is Staging Lethbridge - 4310.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has an open work order invoice {Invoice-A} made at {Location-B}.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST D-39 Dialog.
  • Starting screen: A/R Detail (Reports, then "A/R Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu in light theme at 100% zoom, with {Customer-A} ticked and its rows showing.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
fields.custom_steps:
1. Click {Invoice-A}'s number.
  2. Compare the dialog with the one a work order link from another location shows today.
  3. Click "Cancel".
  4. Switch ShopView to dark theme.
  5. Click {Invoice-A}'s number again.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: a dialog opens over the report; read letter for letter, in order: title "Switch location?", message "This work order is in " then {Location-B}'s name and "Switch your active location to view it?", then the button "Cancel" on the left and the button "Switch location" (small l) on the right, and a close "×" at the top right.
  • Step 2: it is the existing location-switch prompt: same look, buttons and position.
  • Step 3: the dialog closes.
  • Step 4: the page switches to dark theme.
  • Step 5: the dialog opens again and is readable in dark theme.

Where the build is expected to differ: Chris Ward (answer 11, 23 Oct 2026) says the current build writes the button "Switch Location" with a capital L, a build bug to fix; the PRD's "Switch location" stands. No ticket number is known yet. If the button reads "Switch Location", mark this test Failed.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 9 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11537 (Story 7, Document links open where they can)

  • S7-R3: “An invoice or part sale at another location the user is enrolled in shows the existing location-switch prompt on the report, before leaving it: title "Switch location?", message "This work order is in {location}. Switch your active location to view it?" (for a part sale: "This part sale is in {location}. Switch your active location to view it?"), buttons "Cancel" on the left and "Switch location" on the right, and a close × at the top right.”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Click an invoice at another enrolled location | Title "Switch location?", message "This work order is in {location}. Switch your active location to view it?" | Dialog on the report; "Switch location" switches and opens, "Cancel" stays”
  • Key Decisions, reuse rule: “The reuse rule. Every control on these reports reuses an existing ShopView pattern: the native filter chips, the native totals row and pinned headline column of the newer reports, the existing location-switch prompt, the design system's chevron icon. Nothing new is drawn. Basis: d-reuse-existing-pattern.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), read 22 Oct 2026: page 5 "Document links and Switch location" (board Links.dc.html). Compare the screen with the pictures below at 100% zoom; the expected results still come from the PRD quotes above, the pictures give the look and the on-screen labels.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • ar-ap-p5-another-location-asks-first.png: figure "Another location asks first" (This build (after)), board "5. Document links and Switch location (SV-5706)"
  • ar-ap-p5-cancel-stays-on-the-report.png: figure "Cancel stays on the report" (This build (after)), board "5. Document links and Switch location (SV-5706)"

The design's own words:

  • ""Switch location? This work order is in Staging Lethbridge - 4310. Switch your active location to view it?" on the report. Switch Location opens it there. S7-R3, S7-R4." (caption of "Another location asks first")
  • "Same filters, open groups and scroll position. S7-R5, S7-E1." (caption of "Cancel stays on the report")

Difference from the PRD (DD-01), closed: PRD version 5 said buttons "Switch location" and "Cancel" (S7-R3), title "Switch location?"; the design shows buttons "Cancel" (left, grey) then "Switch Location" (right, blue, capital L), and a close "×" at the top right of the dialog; caption: "Switch Location opens it there.". Chris Ward ruled on 23 Oct 2026 (answer 11): the existing prompt keeps "Cancel" on the left, "Switch location" (small l) on the right and a close × at the top right, and the × closes it like Cancel; the capital L the picture and the current build show is a build bug to fix. PRD version 9 (S7-R3, S7-R5) now says so, and this case follows PRD version 9. The held design-version case D-76 (C715558) was deleted from TestRail on 26 Oct 2026 with the QA lead's go-ahead (snapshot in v9-pass-2026-10-26/deleted/).

fields.custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • Scenario: Two customers have overdue invoices, one with a phone number and credit term and one with no phone, on A/R Collection.
  • You are an Admin user (the "Admin" role) working at {Location-A}, your current location.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has an overdue invoice, a phone number and a credit term; customer {Customer-B} has an overdue invoice and no phone.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST D-43 Phone Row with phone (403) 555-0103 and credit term Net 30; {Customer-B} is ZZAUTOTEST D-43 No Phone Row.
  • Starting screen: A/R Collection (Reports, then "A/R Aging Collection" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu in light theme at 100% zoom.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
fields.custom_steps:
1. Read {Customer-A}'s group row, letter for letter.
  2. Read {Customer-B}'s group row, and look for overlap or clipping on both rows.
  3. Switch ShopView to dark theme.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the name, then "Phone: " and the number, then "Credit term: " and the term, on the group row after the name.
  • Step 2: the name and "Credit term: COD" (if none set); no "Phone:" label; on both rows nothing overlaps or is clipped.
  • Step 3: the page switches to dark theme; on both rows nothing overlaps or is clipped.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 9 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11539 (Story 9, A/R Collection call list)

  • S9-R1: “On A/R Collection, each customer's group row shows, after the customer's name, "Phone: " and the customer's phone number as the customer card shows it.”
  • S9-R2: “For users with the 'View and Manage AP/AR Data' switch, the group row also shows "Credit term: " and the customer's credit term as the customer card shows it ("COD" when none is set).”
  • S9-N1: “A customer with no phone shows no "Phone:" label, on screen or in the PDF.”

fields.custom_preconds:

  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
fields.custom_steps:
1. Compare the title row with the picture.
  2. Compare the filter row with the picture, chip by chip.
  3. Compare the column headings with the picture, left to right, letter for letter.
  4. Compare the customer name cells and the money cells with the picture.
  5. Scroll the table down a little and look at the Totals row.
  6. Look at how the table sits on the page.
  7. Widen the browser window to 1536 px and look across the page.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the title "A/R Aging Summary", a grey circled "i" info icon directly right of it, and a grey "⋯" button at the far right, all on one line, as in the picture.
  • Step 2: four chips in this order: "As of: " and the date in a blue pill with a calendar icon and a down arrow; "Customer: All customers" with a person icon and no fill (resting); "Past due: Any" with an hourglass icon and no fill (resting); "Location: All locations" with a location pin icon in a blue pill.
  • Step 3: "Customer" with a small up arrow (the sorted column), "Location", "Current", "1-30 Days", "31-60 Days", "61-90 Days", "91 And Over", "Total", in bold, each on one line; only "Customer" carries an arrow.
  • Step 4: customer names are blue and in A to Z order, a name starting "10" before one starting "2"; money is right-aligned, an empty bucket is blank, a credit shows the minus after the dollar sign (for example "$-100.00"), as today, and the Total column is bold on every row.
  • Step 5: the bold Totals row stays at the bottom of the table while the rows scroll under it, as in the picture.
  • Step 6: the table runs across the page with no card or frame around it, rows divided by thin lines, as in the picture.
  • Step 7: nothing overlaps, is cut off or clipped; the layout is the same as at 1440 px.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 9 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order), story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location), story SV-11536 (Story 6, Location column), story SV-11538 (Story 8, Report descriptions and layout)

  • S8-R2: “The title, its info icon and the Export menu stay on one line at 1440 pixels wide; the filter row sits below them, positioned as on the native reports.”
  • S5-R1: “Each report's filter row is the native report filter row of the newer reports (Inventory Value, Sales By Customer), in this order on all six reports: the date chip ("As of: 10/15/2026"), the customer chip on the A/R reports or the vendor chip on the A/P reports, the Past due chip, then the Location chip.”
  • S5-R13: “The customer chip (A/R) and vendor chip (A/P) and their open menus are the native ones: Customer exactly as Sales By Customer's Customer filter (person icon), Vendor exactly as Inventory Value's Vendor filter (truck icon, "Search vendors"; as there, the search box shows only when there are more than 8 vendors). The menu has a search box, an "All customers" or "All vendors" row, the native line "All customers are included. Pick one or more to narrow." (or vendors) while none is ticked, and the list; several can be ticked. The chip reads "Customer: All customers" or "Vendor: All vendors" in the resting (grey) style when none is ticked, the name when one is (shortened with "..." when long), and "Customer: N customers" or "Vendor: N vendors" when N are. The ticked customers or vendors narrow every row, group, total, page, sort and export; the Location list does not change (S5-R3).”
  • S5-R15: “The Past due chip and its open menu are the same native checkbox dropdown as Customer and Location: label "Past due", an hourglass icon, an "Any" row, the native line "All ranges are included. Pick one or more to narrow." while none is ticked, then "1-30 days", "31-60 days", "61-90 days", "91+ days", in that order; several can be ticked. The chip reads "Past due: Any" in the resting (grey) style when none is ticked, the range when one is (for example "Past due: 91+ days"), and "Past due: N ranges" when N are. Ticking all four reads "Past due: 4 ranges", not Any, because Any also keeps invoices and bills that are not due yet. The ranges are the reports' own aging buckets: 1 to 30, 31 to 60, 61 to 90 and more than 90 days past the due date on the as-of date.”
  • S1-R1: “A/R Summary opens with customers in name order, A to Z; A/P Summary opens with vendors in name order, A to Z.”
